title.en: Prepositions of time: at, on, in
title.es: Preposiciones de tiempo: at, on, in

summary.en: Use **at** for exact times and some fixed expressions (_at 7.30_, _at night_, _at the weekend_), **on** for days and dates (_on Friday_, _on 3 May_) and **in** for longer periods (_in July_, _in 2019_, _in the morning_). Use **no preposition** before _next, last, this, every, tomorrow, yesterday_ and _today_.
summary.es: El español usa «a, el, en» según el caso:«el lunes» = on Monday (sin the), «a las siete» = at seven, «en 2019» = in 2019. Y «la semana que viene» = next week, sin preposición.

form: **at** + clock time and points: _at 9.15, at noon, at midnight, at lunchtime, at Christmas, at night_
**on** + days and dates: _on Monday, on Monday morning, on 12 June, on my birthday_
**in** + months, years, seasons, centuries and parts of the day: _in March, in 2024, in winter, in the evening_
**no preposition**: _next week, last year, this morning, every day, tomorrow, yesterday_
**in** + a period = after that time: _The course starts in two weeks._

uses.text: **Day or date** → on: _The deadline is on Thursday._ _We got married on 21 April._
**Month, year, season, part of the day** → in: _It rains a lot in autumn._ _I read in the evening._

note.en: Exceptions: at night, but in the morning / afternoon / evening; on Friday morning.
note.es: Excepciones: at night, pero in the morning; y on Friday morning.

uses.text: **Holiday periods** → at: _at Christmas_, _at Easter_ (but _on Christmas Day_). In British English: _at the weekend_.
**Time reference words** → no preposition: _I'll call you tomorrow._ _We went to Rome last summer._

mistakes.wrong: The party is in Saturday at the night.
mistakes.right: The party is on Saturday night.

why.en: Use on with days, and say at night or on Saturday night.
why.es: «El sábado» = on Saturday, sin the; y on Saturday night.

mistakes.wrong: I was born at 1995 in the 14th of May.
mistakes.right: I was born in 1995 on 14 May.

why.en: Years take in; dates take on.

mistakes.wrong: I'll see you in the next week.

why.en: Next, last, this and every are used without a preposition or article.
why.es: «La semana que viene» = next week, sin preposición ni the.

mistakes.wrong: On the weekends I usually sleep late.
mistakes.right: At the weekend I usually sleep late. / At weekends I usually sleep late.

why.en: British English uses at the weekend or at weekends.
why.es: En inglés británico: at the weekend / at weekends.

examples.en: The shop opens at nine and closes at half past five.
examples.es: La tienda abre a las nueve y cierra a las cinco y media.

examples.en: My flight is on Sunday morning, so I'll leave at dawn.
examples.es: Mi vuelo es el domingo por la mañana, así que saldré al amanecer.

examples.en: The meeting is on 12 March at 10.30.
It's very hot here in July and August.
I'm usually exhausted in the evening.
We always visit my grandparents at Christmas.
I'll send you the report tomorrow morning.
Last year we didn't have a holiday.
The lecture finishes in about an hour.

practice.prompt: The meeting starts ___ half past nine.
I usually go for a run ___ the evening.

explanation.en: Parts of the day take in, except night (at night).
Next + time word is used without a preposition.

practice.prompt: Many shops stay open late ___ Christmas.

explanation.en: The holiday period takes at: at Christmas.
